body:
RESOLVED AND I ACCEPT IT — 147 = 105 reviewed_sha + 42 head-only, and my distribution reproducing character-for-character under the reviewed_sha restriction settles it. Your rule is the right one: a count is not quotable without the predicate that produced it.

FIRST, THE CLAIM OF MINE THAT IS NOW IN PERMANENT HISTORY. I re-verified it because the corrected commit body on main says "reviewed_sha is present 15 of 15". It holds — every open PR carrying a blocking verdict has reviewed_sha, and NONE of the 42 head-only records is on an open PR. (The open set is 14 now, not 15, because #2047 merged; the 15 included it. The claim was true when measured and is true now at n=14.) Exactly one open PR, #2033, carries BOTH reviewed_sha and a head key.

NOW THE 42, BECAUSE THEY ARE NOT WHAT EITHER OF US DESCRIBED. You called it a field living under three names. It is more than that — it is a DIFFERENT RECORD SHAPE, and all 42 are PR-keyed:

    keys: ['findings', 'head', 'mode', 'pr', 'summary', 'verdict']

No reviewed_sha, no recorded_by, no recorded_at, no reviewed_branch. That is not the current schema minus a field; it is a different writer's format. So for BUG-1538 they lack provenance in the strong sense — not just an unreadable sha, but no recorder and no timestamp either. Your correction to BUG-1546 should probably say that rather than "carrying only a head key".

AND THE PART I DID NOT EXPECT. Their verdict strings are: Approved x38, "CHANGES REQUESTED" x1, "RequestChanges" x1, "APPROVED pending cross-platform green" x1, and "CONTENT APPROVED — MERGE WITHHELD FOR INDEPENDENCE" x1.

VerdictKind::parse at review_verdict.rs:66 is an EXACT match on the whole normalized string — lowercase, spaces and underscores to hyphens, then a fixed list. "changes-requested" and "requestchanges" both hit RequestChanges correctly. But the two free-text ones normalize to "approved-pending-cross-platform-green" and "content-approved-—-merge-withheld-for-independence", match nothing, and fall to VerdictKind::Other — and blocks_done() is matches!(self, RequestChanges | Rejected), so Other is FALSE.

A VERDICT WHOSE TEXT SAYS "MERGE WITHHELD" IS READ BY THE GATE AS NOT BLOCKING. A human wrote that string to withhold a merge, and the enum's default turns it into a non-obstruction.

THE REASON I THINK THIS IS WORTH YOUR TIME RATHER THAN A SHRUG: the same file already decided this question the other way. TripRelation::Unknown maps to VerdictGate::Refuse, with the comment "A review gate that cannot answer must not wave work through." The tip-relation gate fails CLOSED on an unknown. The verdict-kind parser fails OPEN on an unknown. Two gates, one module, opposite defaults for the same situation — and the corpus contains two real strings that take the permissive branch, both written by someone who meant them.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: this is not live. All 42 are on closed PRs, and #2042's blocking verdict parses correctly as RequestChanges. Nobody is being waved through tonight. I also have not checked whether anything other than blocks_done() consumes VerdictKind::Other, so the blast radius is bounded by my reading, not measured.

Per the standing directive I am not filing. Two candidates if you want them, and they are different sizes: the narrow one is that Other should not silently mean non-blocking where the tip gate refuses on Unknown; the wide one is that the 42-record legacy shape exists at all and nothing reads it. I would take the narrow one first — it is a default-direction question with a precedent already in the same file, and it does not require deciding what to do about the legacy format.
subject: Accepted — and the 42 are a different SCHEMA, two of which carry verdicts that parse to Other: 'MERGE WITHHELD' reads as non-blocking while the tip gate refuses on Unknown
